Please analyze this codebase and create a CLAUDE.md file, which will be given to future instances of Claude Code to operate in this repository.
            
What to add:
1. Commands that will be commonly used, such as how to build, lint, and run tests. Include the necessary commands to develop in this codebase, such as how to run a single test.
2. High-level code architecture and structure so that future instances can be productive more quickly. Focus on the "big picture" architecture that requires reading multiple files to understand

Usage notes:
- If there's already a CLAUDE.md, suggest improvements to it.
- When you make the initial CLAUDE.md, do not repeat yourself and do not include obvious instructions like "Provide helpful error messages to users", "Write unit tests for all new utilities", "Never include sensitive information (API keys, tokens) in code or commits" 
- Avoid listing every component or file structure that can be easily discovered
- Don't include generic development practices
- If there are Cursor rules (in .cursor/rules/ or .cursorrules) or Copilot rules (in .github/copilot-instructions.md), make sure to include the important parts.
- If there is a README.md, make sure to include the important parts. 
- Do not make up information such as "Common Development Tasks", "Tips for Development", "Support and Documentation" unless this is expressly included in other files that you read.
- Be sure to prefix the file with the following text:

```
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
```
I'll analyze your codebase and create a CLAUDE.md file to help future instances of Claude Code work effectively in this repository.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Commands

### Development
- `npm run dev` - Start Next.js development server
- `npm run build` - Build production version
- `npm start` - Start production server
- `npm run lint` - Run ESLint

### Environment
The application requires Airtable integration. Key environment variables:
- `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` - Airtable API key
- `AIRTABLE_BASE_ID` - Base ID for the Airtable workspace
- `AIRTABLE_TABLE_QUOTES` - Table name for quotes (default: "Quote Requests")
- `AIRTABLE_TABLE_LINE_ITEMS` - Table name for line items (default: "Quote Line Items")
- `AIRTABLE_FIELD_TOKEN` - Field name for tokens (default: "Token")
- `AIRTABLE_FIELD_QUOTE_ID_LOOKUP` - Lookup field (default: "Quote ID (from Request)")
- `AIRTABLE_FIELD_LINK_TO_QUOTE` - Linked record field name
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` - Optional API base URL for client-side fetching

## Architecture

### Core Structure
This is a Next.js 14 App Router application that serves as a quote viewer for Handld services, integrating with Airtable as the backend data store.

### Key Components
- **Quote Viewer** (`/app/q/[token]/page.jsx`) - Main customer-facing quote display with pricing tiers (standard vs. member pricing)
- **Admin Tools** (`/app/page.jsx`) - Internal testing interface for adding services to quotes
- **Airtable Integration** (`/lib/airtable.js`) - Server-side only utilities for Airtable API operations
- **TotalsStack Component** (`/app/components/TotalsStack.jsx`) - Reusable component for displaying pricing totals

### API Routes Structure
- `/api/quotes/[token]` - GET quote data by token, PUT to update line items and frequencies
- `/api/quotes/[token]/items` - POST to add new line items to quotes
- `/api/health/*` - Various health check endpoints
- `/api/debug/env` - Environment debugging endpoint
- `/api/version` - Version information endpoint

### Data Flow
1. Quotes are identified by unique tokens stored in Airtable
2. Quote data includes both header information (customer details) and line items (services)
3. Line items link to quotes via Quote ID field
4. The system supports both standard and member pricing tiers
5. Frequency selection updates line items and syncs "Selected Services" on quote headers

### Styling
- Uses Tailwind CSS with custom brand colors
- Brand navy color: `#4343B4` (in components) and `#2A54A1` (in globals.css)
- Cream background: `#FFFFF2`
- Responsive design with mobile-first approach

### Client-Side Features
- Resilient API fetching with multiple endpoint fallbacks
- Real-time quote updates when customers select service frequencies
- Debug mode available via `?debug=1` query parameter

content.text:
This is a **Handld Quote Viewer** - a Next.js application that serves as a customer-facing interface for viewing and interacting with service quotes from Handld, a service marketplace company.

## Purpose & User Flow
Customers receive a token-based URL (like `/q/ABC123`) that displays their personalized quote with:
- **Dual pricing tiers**: Standard pricing vs. Handld membership pricing
- **Service selection**: Customers can choose frequency for different services
- **Savings visualization**: Clear display of member savings to encourage membership

## Technical Architecture
- **Frontend**: Next.js 14 with App Router, Tailwind CSS styling
- **Backend**: Airtable as the database via REST API
- **Data Structure**: Quotes contain line items (services) with frequency options
- **Authentication**: Token-based access (no user accounts needed)

## Key Features
1. **Resilient API fetching** - Tries multiple endpoint patterns if one fails
2. **Real-time updates** - Service frequency changes update totals immediately  
3. **Mobile responsive** - Works well on phones for on-site quote reviews
4. **Debug mode** - `?debug=1` shows technical details for troubleshooting

## Business Model Integration
The app is designed to drive Handld membership conversions by clearly showing savings when customers choose the membership pricing tier over standard pricing. It's likely used by Handld sales teams or sent to customers after initial service consultations.

The admin interface (`/app/page.jsx`) suggests this also serves as an internal tool for testing quote modifications.

### API Key

# Handld Quote Viewer Setup

This application requires Airtable integration to function. Follow these steps to configure your environment.

## 1. Get Airtable Credentials

### API Key
1. Go to [Airtable Create Token](https://airtable.com/create/tokens)
2. Click "Create new token"
3. Give it a descriptive name (e.g., "Handld Quote Viewer")
4. Add these scopes:
   - `data.records:read`
   - `data.records:write` 
   - `schema.bases:read`
5. Add access to your specific base
6. Copy the generated token (format: `pat12345abcdef.ghijklmnop.qrstuvwxyz123456`)

### Base ID
1. Open your Airtable base in a web browser
2. Look at the URL: `https://airtable.com/appABCDEF123456789/...`
3. Copy the part that starts with `app` (e.g., `appABCDEF123456789`)

```bash

AIRTABLE_BASE_ID=appABCDEF123456789
```

Perfect! I've successfully refactored the application to use constants instead of environment variables for table and field names. Here's what I accomplished:

## Changes Made

**1. Created a constants file** (`lib/airtable-config.js`)
- All table and field names are now defined as constants
- No sensitive data - just configuration that should match your Airtable schema
- Easy to modify if your Airtable structure differs

**2. Simplified `.env.local`**  
- Now only contains **sensitive credentials**: `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` and `AIRTABLE_BASE_ID`
- Removed all the table/field environment variables
- Much cleaner and less error-prone

**3. Updated main integration files**
- `lib/airtable.js` now imports and uses the constants
- Main API route (`app/api/quotes/[token]/route.js`) updated to use constants
- All field references now use the centralized constants

**4. Enhanced documentation**
- `SETUP.md` now reflects the simplified setup process
- Added guidance on customizing schema names if needed
- Updated troubleshooting section

**5. Improved validation endpoint**
- `/api/setup/validate` now shows both credentials and constants
- Tests actual Airtable connection with the constant table names
- Clearer feedback about what's configured vs missing

## Benefits

- **Simpler setup** - Only 2 environment variables needed instead of 7+
- **Better security** - No non-sensitive data in environment files  
- **Easier maintenance** - Schema changes in one place (`lib/airtable-config.js`)
- **Less prone to typos** - Constants prevent environment variable naming mistakes

You can now test the application by setting just your `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` and `AIRTABLE_BASE_ID` in `.env.local`, and it should work with the standard Handld Airtable schema!

```
[savingsTotal value]
```

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Commands

### Development
- `npm run dev` - Start Next.js development server
- `npm run build` - Build production version
- `npm start` - Start production server
- `npm run lint` - Run ESLint

### Environment
The application requires Airtable integration. Key environment variables:
- `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` - Airtable API key
- `AIRTABLE_BASE_ID` - Base ID for the Airtable workspace
- `AIRTABLE_TABLE_QUOTES` - Table name for quotes (default: "Quote Requests")
- `AIRTABLE_TABLE_LINE_ITEMS` - Table name for line items (default: "Quote Line Items")
- `AIRTABLE_FIELD_TOKEN` - Field name for tokens (default: "Token")
- `AIRTABLE_FIELD_QUOTE_ID_LOOKUP` - Lookup field (default: "Quote ID (from Request)")
- `AIRTABLE_FIELD_LINK_TO_QUOTE` - Linked record field name
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` - Optional API base URL for client-side fetching

## Architecture

### Core Structure
This is a Next.js 14 App Router application that serves as a quote viewer for Handld services, integrating with Airtable as the backend data store.

### Key Components
- **Quote Viewer** (`/app/q/[token]/page.jsx`) - Main customer-facing quote display with pricing tiers (standard vs. member pricing)
- **Admin Tools** (`/app/page.jsx`) - Internal testing interface for adding services to quotes
- **Airtable Integration** (`/lib/airtable.js`) - Server-side only utilities for Airtable API operations
- **TotalsStack Component** (`/app/components/TotalsStack.jsx`) - Reusable component for displaying pricing totals

### API Routes Structure
- `/api/quotes/[token]` - GET quote data by token, PUT to update line items and frequencies
- `/api/quotes/[token]/items` - POST to add new line items to quotes
- `/api/health/*` - Various health check endpoints
- `/api/debug/env` - Environment debugging endpoint
- `/api/version` - Version information endpoint

### Data Flow
1. Quotes are identified by unique tokens stored in Airtable
2. Quote data includes both header information (customer details) and line items (services)
3. Line items link to quotes via Quote ID field
4. The system supports both standard and member pricing tiers
5. Frequency selection updates line items and syncs "Selected Services" on quote headers

### Styling
- Uses Tailwind CSS with custom brand colors
- Brand navy color: `#4343B4` (in components) and `#2A54A1` (in globals.css)
- Cream background: `#FFFFF2`
- Responsive design with mobile-first approach

### Client-Side Features
- Resilient API fetching with multiple endpoint fallbacks
- Real-time quote updates when customers select service frequencies
- Debug mode available via `?debug=1` query parameter

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Commands

### Development
- `npm run dev` - Start Next.js development server
- `npm run build` - Build production version
- `npm start` - Start production server
- `npm run lint` - Run ESLint

### Environment
The application requires Airtable integration. Key environment variables:
- `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` - Airtable API key
- `AIRTABLE_BASE_ID` - Base ID for the Airtable workspace
- `AIRTABLE_TABLE_QUOTES` - Table name for quotes (default: "Quote Requests")
- `AIRTABLE_TABLE_LINE_ITEMS` - Table name for line items (default: "Quote Line Items")
- `AIRTABLE_FIELD_TOKEN` - Field name for tokens (default: "Token")
- `AIRTABLE_FIELD_QUOTE_ID_LOOKUP` - Lookup field (default: "Quote ID (from Request)")
- `AIRTABLE_FIELD_LINK_TO_QUOTE` - Linked record field name
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` - Optional API base URL for client-side fetching

## Architecture

### Core Structure
This is a Next.js 14 App Router application that serves as a quote viewer for Handld services, integrating with Airtable as the backend data store.

### Key Components
- **Quote Viewer** (`/app/q/[token]/page.jsx`) - Main customer-facing quote display with pricing tiers (standard vs. member pricing)
- **LineItemsTable Component** (`/app/components/LineItemsTable.jsx`) - Interactive table showing services with frequency dropdowns and remove buttons
- **Admin Tools** (`/app/page.jsx`) - Internal testing interface for adding services to quotes
- **Airtable Integration** (`/lib/airtable.js`) - Server-side only utilities for Airtable API operations
- **TotalsStack Component** (`/app/components/TotalsStack.jsx`) - Legacy component (replaced by inline totals)

### API Routes Structure
- `/api/quotes/[token]` - GET quote data by token, PUT to update line items and frequencies
- `/api/quotes/[token]/items` - POST to add new line items to quotes
- `/api/health/*` - Various health check endpoints
- `/api/debug/env` - Environment debugging endpoint
- `/api/version` - Version information endpoint

### Data Flow
1. Quotes are identified by unique tokens stored in Airtable
2. Quote data includes both header information (customer details) and line items (services)
3. Line items link to quotes via Quote ID field
4. The system supports both standard and member pricing tiers
5. Frequency selection updates line items and syncs "Selected Services" on quote headers

### Styling
- Uses Tailwind CSS with custom brand colors
- Brand navy color: `#4343B4` (in components) and `#2A54A1` (in globals.css)
- Cream background: `#FFFFF2`
- Responsive design with mobile-first approach

### Client-Side Features
- Resilient API fetching with multiple endpoint fallbacks
- Real-time quote updates when customers select service frequencies
- Debug mode available via `?debug=1` query parameter
